title: Region-bound export playbook: scheduled PDF/CSV evidence delivery with retention enforcement
creator: Aisha Mercado
description: Build a resilient, region-aware export pipeline that generates tenant-scoped compliance artifacts in PDF and CSV formats, attaches signed manifests, validates residency and retention constraints, and delivers via configurable channels on a schedule or on-demand. Provide console dashboards for export status, delivery history, and proof-of-delivery artifacts for audit review.
goals: Support tenant-scoped exports that enforce geographic residency rules at generation time
Produce both PDF (human readable audit pack) and machine-readable CSV exports with consistent schemas
Attach a cryptographic manifest (SHA256 checksums + PGP signature) to each export for non-repudiation
Provide scheduling, retries, and resumable transfers for larger export sets
Expose per-export telemetry and proof-of-delivery in the Redwood Console and tenant dashboards
Allow secure delivery options: tenant S3 bucket push, SFTP, encrypted email with attachment limits, and webhook with signed callback
scope_in: Export orchestration service with residency-aware routing
Export serializers: CSV schema definitions and PDF template generator
Manifest generation and signing flow using customer or Redwood KMS
Delivery adapters: S3, SFTP, SMTP, webhook
Console UI for schedule configuration, export history, and manual replays
Retention policy enforcement at export time and manifest of retained/trimmed records
scope_out: Long-term cold storage lifecycle management beyond delivery (handled by storage teams)
Custom per-tenant legal packaging formats (beyond PDF/CSV) in this phase
Automated downstream ingestion into third-party IR systems (future integration)
Full e-discovery search UI for exported content
risks: Large tenants may generate multi-GB exports causing timeouts or high egress costs
Cross-region export routing mistakes could cause residency violations if not validated
Email delivery may fail for large attachments, requiring coordinated fallback logic
Signing with tenant-managed keys will add complexity to key rotation and failure modes
success_metrics: 90% of scheduled exports complete within SLA windows for exports under 10GB
0 residency violations in production for exports delivered after rollout
Console shows proof-of-delivery and manifest checksums for 100% of completed exports
Reduction in manual evidence requests handled by support by 60% after rollout
notes: PM kickoff 2025-02-11: agreed minimal viable delivery channels S3 and SFTP, plus webhook for API-first tenants
Security flagged tenant-managed keys as a blocker; temporary default signing will use Redwood KMS until key-onboarding flow completes
Discussed incremental export model: export deltas vs full snapshots. MVP will support full snapshots with pagination and resumable chunking
Retention enforcement: exports must include metadata listing which records were excluded due to retention policies and the policy version used
acceptance_criteria: Tenant can create a scheduled export with region selector and delivery target in Console
Export artifacts include PDF and CSV with matching record counts and a signed manifest file
Delivery adapters report success/failure with retry history visible in the export detail view
System rejects any scheduled export whose selected delivery target would violate tenant residency settings
KMS signing verified by independent checksum validation tool and recorded in audit logs
Support runbook documented with steps to replay or redeliver exports and handle partial failures
implementation_notes: Batch export generator should stream CSV rows and incrementally build PDF to avoid OOM for large datasets
Use job checkpoints stored in export-orchestration DB to support resumable transfers
Manifest format: newline-delimited JSON with fields: filename, size, sha256, exported_at, residency_tag
Delivery retries: exponential backoff up to 5 attempts, then escalate to manual retry with notification
Expose export size estimate to tenants in schedule creation to surface egress cost implications
qa_plan: Create synthetic tenant with mixed-region records to validate residency rejection flows
End-to-end test: schedule export, validate manifest signature, deliver to S3, verify object checksums
Failure injections: simulate SFTP interruptions to validate resumable behavior and retry logs
Load test with 50 concurrent scheduled exports to measure orchestration latency and queue behavior
Audit review: security team will perform key rotation test for signing and validate audit log entries
